Article Title: In 2026, an Oregon teen paid $3.07 for a Lakers jacket at Goodwill; Sotheby’s matched it to Wilt Chamberlain’s 1972 Finals run and sold it for $89,600
Article Text:
Wilt Chamberlain. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

A bargain bin find outside Portland

Verifying a jacket worn by an NBA great

From $3.07 to $89,600 at Sotheby's

AI Representation: A vintage Lakers jacket once worn by Wilt Chamberlain. Image credits: Chatgpt

A find that stands out even among thrift store discoveries

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2026, a nineteen-year-old reseller bought a warm-up jacket from a Goodwill store near Portland, Oregon, for $3.07; the jacket later turned out to be Wilt Chamberlain's 1972 NBA Finals jacket, authenticated by Sotheby's and sold for $89,600 at auction. This is yet another addition to an ever-growing list of items found in thrift stores that have proven to be significant sports memorabilia.Quinn Brown, a nineteen-year-old who had been reselling secondhand clothes for three years, was sorting through used clothes at a Goodwill "By-The-Pound" outlet just outside Portland on January 15, 2026, when he noticed a short-sleeved yellow jacket marked "Chamberlain" on the back had been thrown into the bin, according to OPB. He bought the jacket for $3.07 and initially expected to resell it for only a few hundred dollars, as he had found similarly obscure pieces before, according to KPTV. His highest sale to date had been a Sub Pop record-label shirt for $250, reports MyNorthwest. Brown explained that he remembered seeing a Chamberlain warm-up jacket sell for a five-figure sum years earlier, which prompted him to search for pictures of the same jacket online before posting his own find.Chamberlain, inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1978, is considered to be one of basketball’s all-time dominant players based on statistics from the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. In the Sports Hall of Fame , he continues to break NBA records such as scoring 100 points in one game, grabbing 55 rebounds in one game and averaging 50.4 points per game in the 1961-62 season, all records that have remained untouched for over 60 years. Following Brown's post, Sotheby's experts got in touch with him and managed to convince him to sell the jersey at the auction. Through the use of Sotheby’s photomatching technology, it was concluded that the jersey had been worn by Chamberlain during the finals in the 1971-1972 season when he had defeated the New York Knicks in five games to earn himself the title of the MVP of the finals for the first time in his career.Sotheby's set the pre-sale estimate at $150,000–$250,000, describing it on their website as an incredible piece of memorabilia. The final bid came way under this estimate, landing at $89,600, including buyer’s premium, after 48 bids had been placed. Even so, the final price was still a remarkable return on the original $3.07 price tag of the jacket, something few pieces bought in thrift stores can compare to.There was, in fact, a significant gap between Sotheby's estimate and the final bid, with the jacket landing $60,400 below the low end of its $150,000-$250,000 range. Such shortfalls aren't unusual for vintage game-worn memorabilia, since matching a piece to a specific game or series through photos alone is difficult. Brown's jacket, however, was one of the rarer pieces for which Sotheby's photomatching technology succeeded in linking it directly to the 1971-72 Finals.The prolific career of Chamberlain ensures that anything having any connection with him will be collected by somebody. He set the NBA record for career rebounds, with a total of 23,924 rebounds, was twice champion, with the Philadelphia 76ers in 1967 and with the Lakers in 1972, and is a four-time MVP, as stated by the California Sports Hall of Fame. In this light, a jacket associated with his championship period holds far more rarity value than mere career memorabilia.For Brown, the sale was the ultimate jump forward in his collecting career, as he moved from a lifetime of making little money by reselling things to selling one thing that made him a huge profit on the $3.07 that he spent. This also shows that sometimes the most valuable sports memorabilia can be found in a donation box somewhere, waiting to be discovered.
Article Summary: Quinn brown, a 19-year-old reseller, bought a warm-up jacket from a goodwill store near portland, oregon, for $3.07. The jacket later turned out to be wilt chamberlain's 1972 nba finals jacket, authenticated by sotheby's and sold for $89,600 at auction. For brown, the sale was the ultimate jump forward in his collecting career.

Article Title: Tom Brady adds $375M to his fortune with a FOX deal worth nearly $42M more than his NFL earnings
Article Text:
Tom Brady (Image via Getty Images)

Tom Brady's FOX Sports contract eclipses his NFL playing salary

Tom Brady's broadcasting career turns football knowledge into fortune

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady spent 23 seasons building a legendary NFL career, but his biggest financial milestone may have come after he left the field. The seven-time Super Bowl champion is now earning a reported $375 million through his FOX Sports broadcasting deal, surpassing the $332.96 million he collected in NFL playing contracts. For Brady, retirement has opened a new chapter where his football knowledge is proving just as valuable as his playing ability.Brady's reported 10-year, $375 million FOX Sports agreement, signed in 2022, stands out even against the earnings of today's top NFL quarterbacks. The deal made him the network's lead NFL analyst, working alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt.According to Spotrac figures cited by Sporting News, Brady earned around $332.96 million in NFL contracts during his career. His broadcasting deal is worth roughly $42 million more, despite covering a decade rather than 23 seasons.The comparison does not include endorsements, investments or other business ventures. Nor does the $375 million represent an upfront payment. Still, the figures highlight the scale of Brady's second career.His rise makes the contrast even more striking. The New England Patriots selected Brady with the 199th pick in the 2000 NFL Draft.He began as a sixth-round pick with a modest contract, but went on to win six Super Bowls with New England and another with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.Brady also earned three NFL MVP awards, 15 Pro Bowl selections and three first-team All-Pro honours. His highest reported playing earnings came in 2021, when he made about $39.4 million with Tampa Bay.By comparison, his FOX contract averages $37.5 million annually. That puts his broadcasting pay in a league of its own, especially when measured against his career earnings as a player.Brady did not move straight from the field to the FOX booth. He took a year away after his final NFL season before making his broadcasting debut in 2024, calling the Dallas Cowboys' game against the Cleveland Browns with Burkhardt.The transition demanded a different skill set. As a quarterback, Brady could read a defence and react without explaining every thought. Television required him to put those instincts into words for millions of viewers.“To use your voice and vision for a live television audience, there’s a lot of adrenaline in that, but it was very different from when I played. I would probably see all these things, I didn’t have to verbalize them,” Brady said in reflecting on the transition.“I knew subconsciously what to do, and my body just took over because that’s how I trained it. When you embrace the uncertainty, you work as hard as you can to prepare yourself, knowing that you’re going to wish you had done some things over.”His contract also reflects the value networks place on live sports and recognisable talent. A familiar face with deep football knowledge can bring viewers to a broadcast, making top analysts a major investment for media companies.ESPN, for example, recently agreed to a six-year, $108 million extension with Joe Buck, reportedly worth about $18 million per year.Brady, meanwhile, is now in his third season as FOX's lead NFL analyst. His journey from a late draft pick to one of the game's most decorated players helped create the profile behind his broadcasting deal.His playing career built the name. Now, his voice and football insight are generating a remarkable fortune of their own.
Article Summary: Brady's reported 10-year, $375 million fox sports agreement, signed in 2022, stands out even against the earnings of today's top nfl quarterbacks. The deal made him the network's lead nfl analyst, working alongside play-by-play announcer kevin burkhardt. Brady earned around $332.96 million in nfl contracts during his career.

Article Title: 'The place that gave you heartbreak will also give you a reason to smile': Elavenil Valarivan finds a reason to smile in Japan
Article Text:
Elavenil Valarivan (Image: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: Four days ago, when Elavenil Valarivan landed in Japan she carried with her, mixed feelings. The shooter had been to the country before and while that experience may not have been memorable, it was certainly the one to not be forgotten.Elavenil, 27, participated in her first Olympics at Tokyo 2021, where she finished a heartbreaking 16th. While preparing for Aichi-Nagoya, flashes of 2021 returned to her mind, but the shooter, older and wiser now, was able to put them aside.“Thoughts of Tokyo Olympics crossed my mind. It was not a pleasant memory, but over the years, I have trained to put the past behind me and focus on the present. I also told myself that I needed to focus on the Asian Games and not the Olympics,” the shooter told TOI.“I was 22 then and if I had to tell something to my 20-year-old today, I would tell her to be patient and trust the process. I will tell her that the place that gave you heartbreak will also give you a reason to smile about and heal the memories of the past,” she said.‘Ela’ emulated her mentor Gagan Narang, who had also won two silver medals at the 2010 Asian Games. While the mentor was first to call her after her victory, he was also the first to give her some valuable advice.“When I was coming here, he had told me to keep an eye on the weather, the typhoon and plan my bus travels accordingly,” Ela said.In her first Asian Games in 2018, Ela had finished 14th in the same event. The Ahmedabad shooter has been in good form for the past two years and along with the form, other positivity around her has also kept in good shape, mentally. “While on the field, it is the technicality that matters the most. We don’t think about anything that can make us emotional. But off the field, it has been a good phase.”I am happy for my coach Neha (Chavan) ma’am to be nominated for the prestigious Dronacharya Award. She has worked very hard for me, and I am very happy that her efforts have been recognized,” she said.
Article Summary: Elavenil valarivan won two silver medals at the 2010 asian games. The 27-year-old finished a heartbreaking 16th in her first olympics at tokyo 2021. The ahmedabad shooter has been in good form for the past two years.

Article Title: NBA injury update: $40 million Golden State Warriors star gets positive news after devastating first season with the franchise
Article Text:
Kristaps Porzingis injury update. Image via: Getty Images

Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis gets positive health update

Kristaps Porzingis. Image via: USA Today Sports - Imagn

Kristaps Porzingis' first season with Warriors was devastating

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kristaps Porzingis joined the Warriors at the trade deadline as a key piece, and his first stretch in Golden State never got going. Illness and injuries kept taking games away, and the year closed with more questions than answers.The $40 million star has spent the summer insisting the mystery illness is in the past. Now a new assistant coach and the general manager are backing that optimism with their own words, and one of them has a very specific plan for the big man. Media Day arrives on Sept. 28, so the first live answers are close.Kristaps Porzingis has sent the same message all summer. The 2024 NBA champion has said more than once that the "mystery illness" is behind the Latvian, and that a full season feels realistic.The staff now sounds like it agrees. Frank Vogel, the new assistant on Steve Kerr's bench, made it plain. "I'm really excited about putting him in my defensive system," Vogel told Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle. Vogel said the scheme is packed with details he believes in, and that shot-blocking bigs get a lot out of it. He looks forward to putting Porzingis in those spots.On paper, the pairing with Draymond Green stands out. A front line of Porzingis and Green could cause opponents real trouble, particularly if Gui Santos, De'Anthony Melton and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg deliver on the perimeter.Golden State finished 11th in the league on defense last year, and this group projects to be better than average.General manager Mike Dunleavy sees it the same way. The team studied the problem at length, Dunleavy told the Chronicle, looking at how to help and how to do better. The things the staff discussed and worked through, he said, "lean in the direction of him having a healthier year."Camp will offer the first real evidence. Media Day is set for Sept. 28, and the Warriors train at BYU-Hawaii from Sept. 29 through Oct. 3. The team has already signed Nick Boyd, Elias Ralph and Obi Agbim to training camp deals, and the 15-man roster is expected to be final in the first week of October.It is easy to see why the Warriors are welcoming good news. Golden State thought the trade deadline had delivered a key piece, and the closing stretch of the regular season said otherwise.Porzingis missed 16 games over that stretch and played in only 15, thanks to a mix of injuries and illnesses. The Latvian big man was more often out than in, which is a tough way to start life with a new team.The play-in tournament brought a bit of hope and then a setback. Porzingis looked good in the win over the Clippers, a sign of what the Warriors had been hoping to get. Against the Suns, right ankle soreness held Porzingis to 15 minutes in the final play-in loss. Fifteen games to close the regular season, then fifteen minutes in the final play-in game.Golden State opens the preseason against the Clippers in Honolulu on Oct. 4, then starts the regular season against the Lakers on Oct. 21 at Crypto.com Arena.
Article Summary: Kristaps porzingis has spent the summer insisting the mystery illness is in the past. Frank vogel, the new assistant on steve kerr's bench, made it plain. Vogel said the scheme is packed with details he believes in, and that shot-blocking bigs get a lot from it.

Article Title: How Jayden Daniels’ mom supported his football ambitions before the Commanders made him the star QB
Article Text:
Jayden Daniels’ Mom Became a Key Figure in the Quarterback’s Journey (Getty Images)

How did Jayden Daniels' mom shape his path to the NFL ?

Why did Jayden Daniels' mom become a certified NFL agent?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys after dislocating his left elbow on the final play of the first half, the same elbow he injured last November against Seattle. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed it was a left elbow dislocation with no fracture, with more imaging scheduled later this week. The timing is brutal. Daniels was in the middle of one of his sharper performances this season before the play fell apart. Now, as Washington falls to 0-2, attention turns back to the man behind the jersey and the woman who made sure he got there.Jayden Daniels' parents, Regina Jackson and Javon Daniels, met while both were students at Cajon High School in California, the same school their son would later attend. Football was always part of the family DNA. Javon is a big reason Jayden got into the sport at all. "When he was born, when he was old enough to walk, you hand him a ball, and I said, 'this is what you're gonna do,'" Javon said at the Heisman Trophy ceremony.But it was Regina who kept the engine running. "My mother has never missed a game," Daniels said on "The Pivot" podcast. "If it's raining out there, she's going to be out there.If it's minus degrees, she's going to be out there standing up the whole time making sure she's cheering me on." That is not hyperbole. From Arizona State to LSU to the NFL Draft, Regina Jackson showed up. Every single time."The word perseverance is that kid Jayden," she said before the Heisman Trophy ceremony. "The patience he has, the resilience to continue day after day, hour after hour, minute after minute, to be the best version of himself — just watching him get up at 5:30 in the morning to be great is really hard to describe."Daniels has been equally open about how much she means to him off the field too. "Nothing gets past my mama," he said. "She reads people and doesn't put people around me that don't benefit me. My mom's support through this journey has been huge."Regina Jackson did not stop at being a fan in the stands. She became an NFLPA-certified agent after passing the exam administered in late July 2024, making her likely the first parent of a top-three draft pick in NFL history to earn that designation. She holds an MBA with a concentration in entrepreneurship and a master's degree in public service administration. This was not a vanity project."Role number one, she plays my mom. From there, she's my business manager, and then also she is a certified NFL agent," Daniels said. As of March 2026, she became his only listed agent after he parted ways with Agency 1 Sports Group. With a contract extension on the horizon, her role has never mattered more.When Daniels suffered a hamstring injury and fans started drawing comparisons to Robert Griffin III, Jackson quickly shut it down on social media: "I wish you would stop manifesting RGIII on my son. Words are powerful and that's all that's talked about." She protects the narrative as fiercely as she protects his circle.Now, as Daniels heads into another injury scare with Washington needing answers fast, his mother is again at the center of the storm. Not watching from a distance. Right there.
Article Summary: Washington commanders quarterback jayden daniels was carted off the field sunday against the dallas cowboys after dislocating his left elbow. Regina jackson became an nflpa-certified agent after passing the exam administered in late july 2024. She holds an mba with a concentration in entrepreneurship and a master's degree in public service administration.

Article Title: Why Suchika Tariyal lost despite a draw: How 700g denied India’s MMA fighter a historic final and left her in tears
Article Text:
Suchika Tariyal (Video grab)

From an incident at 12 to the Asian Games podium

Judo, Ju-Jitsu and MMA come together

Poll Vote & Share your view Are you optimistic about the future of Indian MMA after Tariyal historic bronze? Very optimistic, more athletes will rise. Not optimistic, it’s still a niche sport. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A historic medal, with a bitter aftertaste

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The medal will go down in Indian sporting history. The manner in which it arrived, however, left Suchika Tariyal in tears.Twenty-four years after an episode of eve-teasing at the age of 12 prompted her to learn how to fight, the 36-year-old from Haryana became India's first Asian Games medallist in mixed martial arts on Monday. But instead of walking away celebrating a landmark achievement, Tariyal was left shattered on the mat after a dramatic semifinal ended in a draw — only for the winner to be determined by a 700-gram difference in the fighters' morning weights.Tariyal and Singapore's Hui Hoon Teo had fought through regulation time and an additional one-minute round without either establishing a decisive advantage. The bout was initially awarded to Teo. The Indian camp challenged the decision, after which the result was changed to a draw.Then came the tiebreak.MMA Sports Federation president Nikhil Kunde told PTI that the winner was determined on the basis of the athletes' morning weigh-in, with Teo around 700 grams lighter than Tariyal. The Singaporean was therefore declared the winner 2-0 and advanced to the gold-medal bout, while Tariyal received bronze.For Tariyal, it was a particularly painful way for her gold-medal hopes to end.She had believed she had done enough to win. Teo had the better of the opening period, but Tariyal fought back strongly in the second. Neither could establish clear superiority in the additional round, although Tariyal managed to take her opponent down just as the buzzer sounded.When the final decision was announced, Tariyal struggled to contain her emotions. She broke down in tears on the mat as her coach tried to console her. She did not immediately go across to shake hands with Teo or the referee.The disappointment was understandable. A few moments earlier, the Indian camp had succeeded in getting the initial verdict changed to a draw. Yet the revised result still did not take Tariyal into the final. A difference of roughly 700 grams ultimately separated the two fighters.And yet, history had already been made.MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, and Tariyal's bronze is India's first-ever medal in the discipline. Her achievement also adds another chapter to one of the most unusual combat-sports journeys in the Indian contingent.Tariyal's journey into combat sports began not with dreams of an Asian Games medal, but with a desire for self-defence.At 12, after experiencing eve-teasing, she decided she wanted to learn how to fight. She took up judo and gradually transformed that initial need for protection into a competitive sporting career.Judo became her foundation. She trained at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and later at the Dada Dev Mandir Centre in Palam before honing her skills at the Sports Authority of India centre in Bhopal.The journey eventually produced eight national judo titles and international success. She won gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games, besides winning silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships. She represented India at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in the women's 57kg category, narrowly missing a medal.But judo was only the beginning.Tariyal moved into kurash and represented India at the 2023 Asian Games. She also took up Ju-Jitsu, eventually becoming world champion in the Adults Ju-Jitsu Contact Female 63kg category at the 2024 JJIF Ju-Jitsu World Championships.Her relationship with MMA had begun earlier, with a debut victory in 2017. She then spent seven years away from the sport while continuing her career in other combat disciplines.When she returned to professional MMA in 2024, she did so with the experience of a fighter who had already spent years building different parts of her game.She made her professional comeback at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain in December 2024 and won. Her subsequent MMA career included national titles and bronze medals at the Asian Mixed Martial Arts Championships in 2026.That multi-discipline background became central to her Asian Games campaign.Tariyal's MMA style was built around the skills she had accumulated over the years — takedowns, grappling, ground control and submissions.Before the Asian Games, she underwent a six-week preparation camp in Mumbai under coaches Nikhil and Sushobhan. She had spoken about how her coaches would wait for her through Mumbai's traffic so she could complete her training and continue refining her techniques.Her preparation showed when she stepped into the Asian Games cage.In Sunday's quarterfinal, Tariyal defeated Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's traditional 60kg category to reach the semifinals. The victory guaranteed India its first medal in MMA because both losing semifinalists received bronze.It was a moment Tariyal had waited years for.“It took me a lot of time to reach here. There is a lot of hard work -- first judo, then other games and now MMA,” she had said after reaching the last four.On Monday, she came within one step of turning that historic bronze into a shot at gold.Instead, the semifinal became a contest decided not simply by what happened inside the cage, but by what the morning weigh-in showed.There is no taking away what Tariyal has accomplished.She has become India's first Asian Games MMA medallist at an edition in which the sport itself is making its debut. At 36, she has added another major milestone to a career that has crossed judo, kurash, Ju-Jitsu and professional MMA.But the circumstances of the semifinal mean the bronze is unlikely to feel complete to her immediately.The Indian challenge had changed the original decision. The bout had become a draw. Tariyal had fought back after losing the opening period and forced the contest into an additional round.Yet the final tiebreak went against her because she was heavier by approximately 700 grams.So the fighter who once took up judo simply because she wanted to learn how to defend herself now stands on an Asian Games podium — but with the memory of a final that was within reach and slipped away on the narrowest of margins.The bronze is historic. The heartbreak is equally real.
Article Summary: Mma is making its asian games debut at aichi-nagoya 2026. Tariyal's bronze is india's first-ever medal in the discipline. The 36-year-old broke down in tears on the mat as her coach tried to console her. She had believed she had done enough to win. Tariyal becomes india's first asian games mma medallist at an edition in which the sport itself is making its debut.

Article Title: How Patrick Mahomes' kids' names - Sterling, Bronze, and Golden tell a hidden story about his career
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes' kids' names - Sterling, Bronze, and Golden tell a hidden story (Getty Images)

Why did Patrick and Brittany Mahomes choose metal-themed names for their kids?

Do Patrick Mahomes' kids' names reflect his Super Bowl legacy?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany are parents to three kids -- Sterling Skye, Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, and Golden Raye, who arrived in January 2025. To most people, these are just unique names. But look a little closer and a pattern appears -- one that connects directly to the metals that define athletic achievement, and quietly mirrors the arc of one of the NFL's most decorated careers.The metallic naming tradition in the Mahomes household did not begin with children. It started with dogs. While still in college, Patrick gifted Brittany a pit bull named Steel -- a nod to the Pittsburgh Steelers. They later added another dog named Silver. By the time their first child came along, the theme had already taken root.Sterling Skye arrived in February 2021, just as Mahomes was cementing himself as one of the most dangerous quarterbacks in the league. Sterling — a reference to sterling silver -- carries a meaning that goes beyond decoration. The word itself signals genuine quality. Something that holds its value. For a quarterback who had already won a Super Bowl MVP before turning 25, the timing felt fitting, even if unintentional.Bronze followed in November 2022, and the story behind that name is more personal. Mahomes has said they were originally going to name their son Trey, since he was Patrick Lavon Mahomes III. It was his brother Jackson who pushed for something different. "He can have his own thing now, where he's not Patrick, he's Bronze," Mahomes explained. The nickname stuck, and with it came an identity separate from the weight of a famous last name.Then came Golden Raye in January 2025 -- the newest member of a family that now numbers five. Gold, in any context, sits at the top. It is the standard everything else gets measured against.The connection is hard to ignore. Sterling, Bronze, Golden -- the three metals of the Olympic podium, and the three children of an athlete who has built one of sport's most dominant dynasties. Whether Mahomes intended it that way is another matter, but the symbolism lands.Laurie Kramer, a professor of applied psychology at Northeastern University, noted that names like these carry dual purpose. "The intention was to build unity in the family," she said. "Everybody's got a metal name in some way, so these kids would feel connected, and it was helping build a family identity around metals which could convey strength and resilience." But Kramer also flagged something worth thinking about: metals come with a built-in ranking. Gold outranks silver. Silver outranks bronze. "When you get names that come with a built-in hierarchy like gold, silver, and bronze, there may be some unintended side effects," she said.Brittany Mahomes has spoken openly about how each name felt right at the time. Sterling was set before they even knew the baby's gender. Bronze evolved naturally once the decision was made to keep the Mahomes name going into a third generation.Golden completed the trio.Together, the three names do something accidental but compelling -- they trace a quiet narrative of a career still being written. Sterling for the early proof of brilliance. Bronze for the continuity of legacy. And Golden, the latest and perhaps most loaded, arriving just as the question of where Mahomes lands all time is being asked more seriously than ever.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes and his wife brittany are parents to three kids -- sterling skye, patrick "bronze" lavon mahomes iii, and golden raye. To most people, these are just unique names. But look a little closer and a pattern appears -- one that connects directly to the metals that define athletic achievement.

Luka Doncic shares heartfelt message to his daughters ahead of Lakers return

Luka Doncic shares honest take on his growth on and off the court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Luka Doncic left basketball out of his newest Instagram post and wrote to his two daughters instead. He shared it on Sunday, after spending a big part of the offseason in Slovenia and getting back to Los Angeles.The note was short and carried no news about the team. Even so, the calendar gives it weight. Lakers media day is Sept. 28, and training camps around the league open the next day. The Slovenian picked his family as the audience before any of that began, and he kept the words plain.The Sept. 20 post was written in Slovenian. Translated into English, its main line reads: “Wherever I go, you are always with me. I love you!”G+O, the daughters' initials, sits at the top of the caption. Doncic also told them that being apart will not change where they stand in his life. Two heart emojis wrap it up. Nothing in it points to the season or his workouts. It reads like a dad checking in, and little else.His daughters were already part of his summer plans. As Reuters reported in May, he chose to skip Slovenia's national-team duty to have more time with them. The 2025-26 season had ended without him on the floor for the playoffs, since a left hamstring injury sidelined him.The Lakers star also used Ljubljana as a small training base. In August, he brought teammates together there for bonding and a pair of casual practices. September brought his own conditioning and court work in the same city. The August meetups gave the group a head start on familiarity before the official preseason.Coach JJ Redick will soon start testing how the roster works around Doncic, and the rotation will take shape from there.Doncic enters this season as the lone headliner in Los Angeles, with LeBron James gone. In an interview with SLAM, he talked about how he has changed. His answer was modest, “probably a better basketball player, more mature.” The way he plays, smile included, is much the same, he added.Madrid is where his pro career started. From there he moved to the NBA and was ranked among its best in short order. Going pro early was not easy, yet he credits it with pushing him to mature faster than most players.Dallas is part of the growth story as well. Boston beat the Mavericks in the 2024 NBA Finals, and Doncic was the one leading Dallas there. Doubts about his leadership, and about whether he could win a title, followed.Los Angeles has already seen the fun side. In one full season with the Lakers, fans and teammates noticed his lively personality, the way he needles opponents and hunts for any competitive edge.
Article Summary: Lakers star luka doncic left basketball out of his newest instagram post and wrote to his daughters. He shared it on sunday, after spending a big part of the offseason in slovenia. Lakers media day is sept. 28, and training camps around the league open the next day.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal challengers bengaluru (rcb) beat chennai super kings (csk) in ipl 2026 encounter at the m chinnaswamy stadium. Tim david, rajat patidar and devdutt padikkal hit 70, 48 and 50 respectively to lift rcb to 250/3. Bhuvneshwar kumar took 3-41 as csk were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs.

Article Title: 'Life is a marathon, not a sprint,' says Tata Sons’ Chandra
Article Text:
Chandrasekaran was delivering his address at SAI University in Chengalpattu

Chennai:“Life is a marathon race, not a sprint. It is about becoming better by the day, not overtaking others. There will be ups and downs. Don’t fear downs, and do not turn your confidence into arrogance. Enjoy the journey,” Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran said on Saturday.Delivering his address at SAI University in Chengalpattu, he said: “It applies to both sports and life. It is all about the willingness to put in the effort to prepare, and not about winning. Understanding what it takes to win is crucial.”Stating that he himself is a runner, a hobby he took up 18 years ago, he advised students to run for themselves with a clear target in mind.Chandrasekaran said the world was full to the brim with possibilities, though it was rapidly changing, disruptive, and increasingly AI-led.“It may be unnerving to read through the negative stories about job losses due to AI and so on. But a number of new sectors are opening. The art of the possible is becoming clear every day with AI and it is going to throw up so many things we have not imagined today. New industries will come up in the next five years, but we may not even know their terminology yet.And India is in a very strong position. India’s economic growth will be unparalleled in our own history and in any part of the world,” he said.Chandrasekaran urged the young generation to keep learning and use social media to their benefit. “Make sure you read, watch and listen to what you choose to,” he said.“To earn the right to feel the pressure is a privilege,” he said, quoting tennis legend Billie Jean King. Pressure would be a constant in one’s life after graduating from college and youngsters should learn to enjoy it all through their life, he said.
Article Summary: Chandrasekaran was delivering his address at sai university in chengalpattu. He said the world was full to the brim with possibilities, though it was rapidly changing. He urged the young generation to keep learning and use social media to their benefit.

Article Title: Marvel's Wolverine hotfix finally dims the scent trails
Article Text:
Insomniac has reduced the opacity of Marvel's Wolverine's Scent Trails and Audio Sense indicators in update 1.001.005, with a full toggle still under consideration.

A full off switch is on the table, but Insomniac has not committed to one

Insomniac Games has rolled out the first fix for the most mocked part of Marvel's Wolverine. Update 1.001.005, released on 18 September, reduces the opacity of the game's Scent Trails and Audio Sense indicators so the glowing paths that steer Logan toward his next objective sit lighter on screen. The studio describes the change as making the visuals "less intense". The same download also clears a set of crashes that a small share of players had been running into since launch.The trails, nicknamed fart trails by players, became the lightning rod for a broader complaint. Critics argued that a linear action game does not need constant signposting, and that the combination of trails, on-screen markers and prompting voice lines left almost nothing in the level for the player to work out.The patch notes say the team is still evaluating ways to improve the Senses systems, including toggleable options in a future update. No date is attached, and no promise has been made that the trails can be turned off completely. A separate UV bug is also queued for a fix, according to community and marketing director James Stevenson, who said ahead of release that the team had been "cooking hard" on feedback.Marvel's Wolverine is a PS5 exclusive and currently sits as the lowest-rated single-player AAA release from a PlayStation first-party studio since Days Gone in 2019. Player scores on PSN and aggregator sites have landed noticeably higher than review scores.For now, the guidance is quieter rather than gone. Whether it disappears entirely is a decision Insomniac has pushed to a later patch.
Article Summary: Insomniac games has rolled out the first fix for the most mocked part of marvel's wolverine. Update 1.001.005 reduces the opacity of the game's scent trails and audio sense indicators so the glowing paths that steer logan toward his next objective sit lighter on screen.
